newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica JSE turnover up 51.7 pct to end-March 1997.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica JSE turnover up 51.7 pct to end-March 1997.

text.p: Turnover on South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), excluding arbitrage deals, surged 51.7 percent in the three months ended March 1997 compared to the same period last year, the bourse said on Friday.
The JSE said trade worth 41.25 billion rand has been concluded since the start of the year until March 27, compared with 27.20 billion rand in the same period in 1996.

It said its market capitalisation had risen by 9.3 percent in the first three months of this year and stood at 1,211 billion rand at the end of March. On that date last year it stood at 1,108 billion rand.
In U.S. dollar terms the JSE's market capitalisation was worth $268.85 billion on February 28, 1997 and was ranked 15th largest in the world.

Ranked by dollar turnover, the JSE, at end February 1997 rose to 28th position among the 45 member stock exhanges of the Federation Internationale des Bourses de Valeurs from 32nd position at the end-January 1997.
Its liquidity ratio at the end of February rose to 14.2 percent from 11.2 percent, giving it a position of 38 from 39 a year ago.
For the month ended March 1997, liquidity improved to 12.3 percent from 8.8 percent in the same period last year, reflecting an increase of 40 percent.

The JSE said net foreign purchases on the bourse stood at 3.47 billion rand for the first three months of 1997. Net foreign buys of shares for the whole of 1996 stood at 5.25 billion rand and 4.81 billion rand in 1995.
